title: ORACLE: what survives a PERFECT reference? Give the judge the answer key and see whether the frontier resolves (596 calls)
question: The same 302 arx / iask discriminating questions, same judge, rubric and v2 mechanics as ARXIASK, pairwise dual order; the single manipulation is the reference block (ground-truth letter and option text), wrapper sentence byte-identical; (1) accuracy vs the 0.612 the grok reference scored; (2) recover the arx > iask order at p < 0.05; (3) paired McNemar vs ARXIASK; (4) irreducible error; at or below 0.70 the through-line would be falsified; prediction 0.78-0.88.

plain_description.what: On 302 hard questions where two frontier models differ, the judge was given the true answer key as its reference instead of a grok-written reference, with everything else unchanged (596 calls).
plain_description.why: It measures how much judge error comes from imperfect references versus the judge itself, and whether a perfect reference resolves the frontier ordering.
plain_description.information: A big gain that recovers the right order would say references are the bottleneck. A residual error would point at the judge's own behaviour. Result: done. A perfect reference raised accuracy from 61.2% to 77.7% but still did not recover the correct order of the two models. Most remaining errors were ties, and committed errors mostly favoured the longer answer. The judge's own error was the larger part, so 'the reference is the binding constraint' is too strong. Later ruled history, not evidence, for the current thesis (old data family).
